analysis.visual_description: On the part. A part lies on the table in the chamber. The oath is the block of lines at the top. The rest of the sheet runs on and is not the thing he is looking at.
On the part. Under those three lines, in his own hand, a plain sentence that is not verse. The pen is capped. Gib is not in the frame.
On the part. The corner of the same sheet. One line, the hour, nothing about a tally.
